name: Mill Creek / Avon — Existing Goodwill Store

meta.sourceModel: Basic property pull only, benchmark/reference card — per B. Blackburn 8/19/26, economics and scenarios intentionally left off pending further direction.

thesis.v: Goodwill's existing 10,260 SF store and donation center at 34 Mill Creek Dr (built 2015, on a 0.90-acre pad at the Avon Street Extended corner) — this card exists purely as the comparison Jackson Green (Goodwill CFO) asked for in the 8/19 email thread, and as the reference point for cannibalization risk and store-format sizing against the 5th Street and Pantops expansion candidates. Avon St Ext at Mill Creek carries 11,000–12,000 ADT, about 70% lighter than 5th Street SW's 19,000 ADT — the direct answer to Jackson's question. GIS confirms the store fronts Mill Creek Drive at its Avon Street Extended corner, resolving an earlier geocoder ambiguity about which end of Mill Creek Drive the address sits on. This store sits inside the 5th Street site's trade area (1.6 miles apart) but well outside Pantops' (3.6 miles), so cannibalization risk reads meaningfully higher for a 5th Street expansion than for Pantops. Not itself a deal under evaluation — no financing model or development scenario applies here.

flags.text: This is the comparison Jackson Green asked for: Avon St Ext at Mill Creek carries 11,000 ADT (12,000 weekday) versus 19,000 ADT (21,000 weekday) on 5th St SW at the Carter Bank site — 5th Street is roughly 70% heavier.
BENCHMARK SIZE: 10,260 SF, built 2015, single story on a 0.90-acre pad — this is the store format the two candidate sites (5th Street, Pantops) should be measured against.

Highest one-mile median household income of the three sites ($112,758) and the only one that is majority owner-occupied inside a mile (59%) — a favorable donation-supply profile for this existing store, despite the smallest one-mile population (4,222).

Address discrepancy worth a quick note, not a real risk: Albemarle County GIS lists the property's street number as 36 Mill Creek Dr, not 34 — same parcel, same corner, almost certainly a minor addressing variance rather than a different property.

1.6 miles from the 5th Street site and 3.6 miles from Pantops — the 5th Street site sits inside this store's existing trade area, Pantops largely does not. Read this as a stronger cannibalization concern for 5th Street than for Pantops.

extras.label: Why this card exists
extras.text: Not a deal under evaluation — this is a benchmark/reference card for the 5th Street and Pantops expansion analysis, built to directly answer Jackson Green's (Goodwill CFO) 8/19 request to compare 5th Street traffic against "counts on Avon at Mill Creek," and to give the other two candidate sites a real store-format size to be measured against. Economics, rent, and scenario analysis are intentionally excluded, as with the other two cards.

extras.label: Demographic methodology note
extras.text: Ring demographics (ACS 2019–2023 5-year estimates) are aggregated by block-group centroid falling inside each radius — block groups aren't split at the ring boundary, so small rings are approximate. Median household income is a household-weighted average of block-group medians, not a true ring median.
